title: Some neutron stars emit beams of radiation from their magnetic poles.
purpose: Set up the concept of pulsars.
narration: Some neutron stars spin incredibly fast and have powerful magnetic fields. These fields funnel particles into beams that shoot from the magnetic poles. As the star rotates, the beams sweep across space like a lighthouse. When a beam points toward Earth, we detect a pulse of radiation. That's what we call a pulsar.
